summary.one_liner: Qwen3-TTS is Qwen's family of open speech generation models (0.6B and 1.7B) that cover custom voices, voice design from text descriptions, voice cloning, and a companion speech tokenizer.
keywords: clone my voice from a short clip
make an audio narration from text
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a series of Qwen3-TTS models released as 0.6B and 1.7B variants: CustomVoice (preset speakers steered by instructions), VoiceDesign (voice created from a natural-language description), and Base (3-second voice cloning from reference audio, also usable for fine-tuning). A separate Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz encodes speech into codes and decodes them back to audio. The qwen-tts Python package exposes generate_custom_voice, generate_voice_design, and generate_voice_clone functions, with single and batch inputs, and reusable voice-clone prompts. A Gradio-based local web UI is started with a qwen-tts-demo command. The README also documents vLLM-Omni offline inference examples, a fine-tuning repo reference, a DashScope API, and benchmark tables for WER, speaker similarity, and tokenizer quality.
use_cases: generate speech audio from text in multiple languages
clone a speaker's voice from a short reference clip
design a new voice from a text description
build a consistent character voice across many lines
run a local web demo for text to speech
fine-tune a TTS model on custom voices
notable: Single model supports both streaming and non-streaming generation, with end-to-end latency the README gives as low as 97ms
Voice design from natural-language instructions, with a documented workflow to turn a designed voice into a reusable clone prompt
Ships 9 preset speakers with per-speaker native-language notes, covering dialects such as Beijing and Sichuan
Custom Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz codec built on a multi-codebook discrete LM architecture rather than LM+DiT
caveats: FlashAttention 2 needs compatible hardware and only works with float16 or bfloat16; the README suggests MAX_JOBS=4 on machines with under 96GB RAM
Base-model web demo should be served over HTTPS for microphone access, using a self-signed cert for testing
vLLM-Omni support is offline-only for now; online serving is stated as future work
The DashScope API documentation links in the README are empty in the provided text, and the README states other technical-report models will be released later
